title: Novigrad with a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules, Heat, Vets
metaDescription: Planning a trip to Novigrad, Istria with a dog: dog beaches, restaurant and old town rules, hotel pet fees, best months, vet tips and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Dog Beaches in Novigrad (Plaža za Pse)

Novigrad has several dedicated dog beaches, which is unusual for a small Istrian town.

- **Dog Dreams Beach & Bar, Kastanija.** The most popular option. It is a beach bar built for dogs, with dog beds in different sizes, dog showers, fresh water bowls, waste bins and plenty of shade. The bar serves alcohol-free dog beer and dog ice cream in salmon, chicken and beef flavours, plus drinks and small snacks for owners. It is listed as open daily from 10:00 to 22:00. Hours can change by season, so check before a special trip.
- **Kostanjija (Kastanija) dog beach.** Gravel and rock, with natural shade and a drinks stand nearby. Entry is free.
- **Campsite dog zones.** Aminess Sirena campsite has a marked area for dogs to stay and swim. Aminess Maravea Camping Resort and Aminess Laguna hotel have the same. Confirm day-visit access with the operator.

Bring water, a towel and a shade cover. The surfaces are gravel and rock rather than sand, so check paws on hot days. Dog Dreams is the best choice for a first visit.

## Are Dogs Allowed on Other Beaches?

On most official public beaches in Croatia, dogs are not permitted in the main season unless the beach is explicitly marked as dog-friendly. Assume "no dogs" at any swimming beach without a dog sign, and use the designated beaches above. Cleaning up after your dog is mandatory, and fines apply. In the shoulder season, rocky coves outside the town centre are quieter, but local rules and signs still apply.

## Old Town, Restaurants and Cafés

Novigrad's old town sits on a small peninsula and is compact: the whole walled centre takes about 15 minutes to walk. Dogs on a lead are normal on the waterfront promenade and in the lanes. Stone paving gets very hot in July and August, so walk early morning or after sunset.

Outdoor terraces in Croatia generally welcome dogs. Indoor access depends on the owner and staff. Dogs are not allowed in shops selling food or in supermarkets. Ask before sitting down, and keep your dog under the table.

## National Parks, Ferries and Catamarans

Novigrad has no national park of its own. Parks elsewhere in Croatia (Plitvice, Krka, Brijuni, Kornati) restrict or ban dogs in most areas, so check each park's rules first. In Istria, dogs are much easier to manage on coastal paths and in the countryside, and Kamenjak near Premantura is known as a dog-friendly area.

Novigrad has no regular passenger ferry of its own. If you extend the trip to the islands, Jadrolinija carries pets free of charge on its ferries. Dogs stay on the open deck on a lead and muzzled, and are not allowed in lounges, restaurants or indoor seating. Catamarans are stricter. Dogs over about 8 kg may need a paid, reserved open-deck box, and the price is given on request. Choose a conventional car ferry for a large dog.

## Accommodation: What a Dog Costs

Pet fees in Croatia vary widely. Hotels commonly charge €10–€40 per night. Private apartments often charge €5–€25 per night, and some charge nothing or a flat fee of about €50–€70 per stay. Many properties limit dogs to 10–25 kg and one or two per room. Private holiday apartments with a garden or terrace are usually easier and cheaper for dogs than hotels. Always confirm the fee and weight limit in writing before booking, because the listed policy and the host's actual practice sometimes differ.

## Best Months and Summer Heat

The best months are May, June and September: warm sea, fewer crowds and manageable temperatures. April and October are good for walking, but the sea is cool. July and August are the hardest. Pavements and gravel burn paws, and a dog should never be left in a parked car. Plan walks before 09:00 and after 19:00, rest in shade at midday and carry water at all times.

Save your money on a hotel room with a pool in peak summer. A shaded apartment near Kastanija and a day at Dog Dreams gives a dog far more than a pool it cannot use.

## Vet Basics

Register a nearby vet before arrival; Poreč and Umag are the larger towns near Novigrad. Carry the passport, vaccination records and your home vet's number. Check for ticks after every countryside walk. Ask your vet about tick and sandfly protection before leaving, because Istria's summer parasite load is real. Check the sea and shoreline for jellyfish and for algae warnings. Fresh water after each swim stops dogs licking salt off their coats.

## EU Pet Passport and Entry Rules

Dogs from EU countries need an ISO 11784/11785 microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport issued by an authorised vet. The microchip must be implanted before, or on the same day as, the rabies vaccination. After a first rabies vaccination, wait 21 days before travelling. Croatia does not require tapeworm treatment for dogs and has no quarantine for correctly documented pets. Owners from outside the EU, such as the UK, need an Animal Health Certificate instead of an EU passport. Pet passports are issued only to owners whose main home is in an EU member state. Start the paperwork at least a month before departure. Check any national rules on breeds and dog numbers in your transit countries.

## Verdict: How Dog-Friendly Is Novigrad?

Novigrad scores 8 out of 10 for dogs. Its dedicated dog beaches (Dog Dreams, Kastanija, the Aminess zones) are a real strength, the old town is walkable, and the terraces are welcoming. The limits are the same as in the rest of Croatia: dogs are barred from ordinary beaches, hot paving in summer, and no national parks nearby. It is a very good base for a relaxed holiday with a dog, especially in May, June and September.

faq.question: Does Novigrad, Croatia have a dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Dog Dreams Beach & Bar in Kastanija is the best known, and there is a Kastanija dog beach. The Aminess Sirena, Maravea and Laguna properties also have marked dog zones.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed on normal beaches in Croatia?
faq.answer: Usually not in the main season, unless the beach is explicitly marked as dog-friendly. Use designated dog beaches and check local signs. Owners must clean up after their dog or risk a fine.

faq.question: Can dogs go to restaurants in Novigrad?
faq.answer: Terraces generally welcome dogs on a lead. Indoor seating depends on the venue and staff, so ask first. Dogs are not allowed in food shops.

faq.question: What documents does a dog need to enter Croatia from the EU?
faq.answer: A microchip (ISO 11784/11785), a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport. The chip must come before or on the same day as the vaccine, and a first vaccination needs a 21-day wait before travel.

faq.question: Do dogs travel free on Croatian ferries?
faq.answer: On Jadrolinija ferries, pets travel free of charge. Dogs must stay on the open deck, on a lead and muzzled. Catamarans can require a paid box for dogs over about 8 kg, so ask before booking.

faq.question: When is the best time to visit Novigrad with a dog?
faq.answer: May, June and September are best. July and August are hot, with hot paving and gravel, so walks should be early morning or evening.

quickAnswer: Novigrad is dog-friendly, mainly thanks to its dog beaches: Dog Dreams Beach & Bar in Kastanija, the Kastanija dog beach and the marked dog zones at the Aminess campsites. The old town is easy to walk on a lead, and terraces usually welcome dogs. Visit in May, June or September. EU travellers need a microchip, rabies vaccination and a pet passport.
